To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) the informativeness of word parts can be used to predict the eye-movement pattern of the reader and (2) the informativeness is used by the reader to guide his or her eye movements.
reading words with informative beginnings is more efficient than reading words with informative endings.
reading words embedded in sentences can be influenced by their informativeness.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the word as a unit in the reading process.
the question of how the information structure of a word influences the way in which it is processed during the course of reading.
the influence of the informativeness of specific word regions on the eye movements made during reading and comprehension of text.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the eye movement behavior is influenced by the information distribution within a word, and that the influence is stronger when reading for comprehension than when reading for lexical identification.
the informativeness within the word is used as a cue for the selection of a convenient viewing point.
the informativeness and the position of a word within a sentence are both important factors in eye movement behavior during reading.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the informativeness and redundancy of a word region can be a factor influencing fixation behavior.
the reader has a strong tendency to fixate on informative regions within a word, especially when the word is embedded in a sentence.
lexical information is used in reading in two ways.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the informativeness within a word can affect the reading process.
the eye-mind assumption can be extended to the notion that the eye is sensitive to information embedded within words.
the eye movement patterns of skilled readers can be modulated by the information content of the words being processed.
